name: Hydrogen atom
headline: bohrRadius
subtitle: Sized by the Bohr radius
description: Hydrogen is the simplest atom, made of a single proton and a single electron. An atom has no hard edge, so its size is usually expressed through the Bohr radius, a fundamental physical constant that sets the natural length scale of the hydrogen atom. The CODATA 2022 value published by NIST is about 5.29 x 10^-11 m, a little over half of a ten-billionth of a metre.

measures.label: Bohr radius
measures.note: CODATA 2022 recommended value of the Bohr radius a0, 5.291 772 105 44(82) x 10^-11 m; standard uncertainty 0.000 000 000 82 x 10^-11 m (relative 1.6 x 10^-10). Used as the atom's radius, so the drawing is twice this wide.

facts.text: NIST lists the Bohr radius with a relative standard uncertainty of 1.6 x 10^-10, making it one of the most precisely known lengths in physics.

caveats: An atom has no sharp boundary; the Bohr radius is a defined length scale (the electron's orbit radius in the Bohr model of hydrogen), not a measured edge, so drawing the atom as a disc of this radius is a convention.
No sourced mass for a hydrogen atom in kilograms was fetched, so mass is left out.
